niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want psychological self-inquiry, a structured meditation practice, or a tradition-based spiritual path. These are good starting points based on the available course information:

### For Jungian shadow work
- **Jung Platform — *Encounters with the Shadow***: A strong starting point if you want shadow work grounded in Jungian depth psychology. It features Jungian analyst James Hollis and is described as suitable for beginners as well as more experienced learners. [Course details](https://jungplatform.com/course/encounters-with-the-shadow)
- **Jung Platform — other shadow courses**: The platform also lists courses with teachers including James Hollis, Craig Chalquist, and Ken James, covering personal and collective shadow, relationships, and dreams. Browse the [shadow-work courses](https://jungplatform.com/shadow-work) and compare the focus of each.
- **Live group courses**: These can offer structure and discussion, but check the facilitator’s training, group boundaries, and whether the course is educational or therapeutic before enrolling.

### For a steady spiritual practice
- **Tara Brach and Jack Kornfield — *Mindfulness Daily***: A 40-day online mindfulness and meditation training. A practical choice if you want a guided daily routine. [Course details](https://courses.tarabrach.com/courses/mindfulness-daily)
- **Naropa University — personal-enrichment courses**: Offers online material on mindfulness and Buddhist practice, including a free introductory course on mindfulness and its roots, plus longer study-and-practice series. [Course details](https://www.naropa.edu/academics/personal-enrichment/)
- **Mindful.org courses**: A broad selection of online mindfulness and meditation courses from different teachers; useful if you want to compare approaches. [Browse courses](https://www.mindful.org/courses/)

**A sensible path:** Start with an introductory Jungian shadow-work course and a gentle daily meditation course, rather than taking an intensive program in both at once. Shadow work can bring up difficult emotions; choose a course that encourages pacing and support, and consider working with a licensed mental-health professional if it becomes overwhelming. These courses can support reflection and spiritual practice, but they aren’t a substitute for therapy.
